title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II
summary: Given an array of length n, sorted in ascending order and rotated between 1 and n times, find the minimum element.
statement: Given an array of length n, sorted in ascending order and rotated between 1 and n times, find the minimum element. The array may contain duplicates. Ensure the operation steps are minimized.
constraints: 1–5000 integers from -5000 to 5000 form a rotated nondecreasing array. Duplicates are allowed; a full rotation may leave the array sorted.
Return the minimum value, not its index. Eliminate half the search interval whenever comparisons allow; equal endpoints may require shrinking one position.
target_time_complexity: O(log n) without ambiguous equalities; O(n) worst case with duplicates
hints: Compare the midpoint with the right edge of the remaining rotated interval.
A larger midpoint puts the minimum to its right; a smaller midpoint keeps the midpoint and left side.
On equality, discard only the rightmost duplicate. Continue until left and right meet.
Duplicates make an O(n) worst case unavoidable for this comparison strategy; distinct values retain O(log n) behavior.
editorial: Maintain an interval containing a minimum. Midpoint comparisons against its right edge normally eliminate half. Equality cannot determine which side contains a smaller value, but deleting the rightmost equal copy preserves at least one minimum. The independent oracle performs a full minimum scan. This is distinct from target searching: there is no target argument and the result is a minimum value. Without duplicate ambiguity, the same reference takes logarithmic time; all-equal inputs illustrate its linear worst case.

tests.explanation: A full rotation leaves the array sorted, so its minimum is the first value, 1.
The repeated 2 values do not identify the pivot; the minimum 0 is inside the array.
